Higher prices may turn out to be the smaller problem. A supply crunch would be worse. Every European Union member state has an obligation to secure enough natural gas ahead of winter to fill 80% of storage capacity. Germany has failed to do that, only filling its storage to about 61%. analysis.summary: Germany missed its winter gas storage target at only 61% capacity amid soaring European natural gas prices.
analysis.rationale: While directly concerning natural gas, severe winter gas shortages and high prices can trigger gas-to-oil switching for heating and power, exerting upward price pressure on crude oil.

news.title: Global refinery inputs fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 before modest recovery
news.summary: Global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), or 6%, following the start of conflict in late February in the Middle East, according to data from Kpler. Throughput then increased by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, primarily as refiners in the region adjusted to new trade flows.

analysis.summary: Global refinery crude inputs fell sharply by 4.8 million b/d in 2Q26 following Middle East conflict before partially recovering by 1.8 million b/d in 3Q26.
analysis.rationale: A substantial net reduction in refinery throughput signals lower crude oil processing demand, exerting downward pressure on crude prices despite the partial rebound. Prompt market context showed slight price declines following publication.

news.title: IEA Warns Global Gas Crunch Could Last Well into 2027
news.summary: The global gas market could remain tight well into next year as Europe enters the heating season with the lowest levels of gas in storage in over a decade, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said in a new report on Tuesday. analysis.summary: The IEA warned that global natural gas markets could stay tight through 2027 due to low European storage and Strait of Hormuz disruptions.
analysis.rationale: Severe natural gas tightness heading into winter and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz typically encourage gas-to-oil switching and elevate energy risk premiums, though the report focuses primarily on gas.
